analysis: Both changed files are documentation only: changelog.d/delta-complete-checkpoints.md (line 3) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (one added table row at head line 1960, in the env-var table). No executable code, auth, crypto, or wire protocol is modified in the supplied evidence, so no control regression is visible. The changelog adds a statement that DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS=0 is copied into the launchd job by `darkbloom start` and kept by `darkbloom restart`. The CLI reference documents the same variable, pointing at SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift (`incrementalCheckpoints`), with 0/false/no/off writing complete checkpoints. This touches T-041 (the SSD prefix cache, TB-007). The delta-checkpoint feature itself (partial files plus recurrent state) is described but its implementation is not in the supplied diff. Any security effects of delta files on the DBK3 AAD, HMAC lookup tag, cacheSalt scoping, TTL/LRU behavior, or restore-chain integrity cannot be assessed here, and that code lives in other PRs or commits. Open integration questions: (1) whether delta files remain bound to the same salt, model, and weightHash, and whether a missing parent file expires or fails closed on restore; (2) whether the launchd env forwarding is a rollback-only switch that cannot weaken isolation. This variable only switches between delta and complete writes and does not touch the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. Claims in the docs are unverified against source. No threat-model update is needed from these docs alone, though the T-041 affected_files and detection_hint could later mention delta checkpoints if the implementation changed the on-disk format.
